topics.title: A program needs exactly one main
topics.body: `main` is the entry point the runtime calls; a second definition fails at link time because the symbol would exist twice.

topics.title: Source becomes an executable in stages
topics.body: Preprocessing, compilation, assembly and linking each produce a different file; `g++` runs all four unless told to stop earlier.

topics.title: The toolchain has four stages
topics.body: Each stage has a flag that stops the build: `-E` preprocesses, `-S` emits assembly, `-c` emits an object file and the default links.

topics.title: A comment records the reason
topics.body: The code already says what happens; a comment earns its place by explaining why, as in the tax rule below.

topics.title: A build fails before it runs
topics.body: A compile error stops the pipeline, so no executable exists to run. Reading the first diagnostic is faster than reading the last.

topics.title: cin skips whitespace between fields
topics.body: Extraction ignores leading whitespace, which is why two integers separated by spaces can be read one after another.

topics.title: Insertion chains left to right
topics.body: `std::cout << a << b` feeds the stream from each expression to the next, so order of appearance is order of printing.

topics.title: setfill chooses the padding character
topics.body: `setw` sets the width of the next field and `setfill` chooses what fills it; the fill persists after the field is printed.

topics.title: A newline is a character
topics.body: `\n` is one character with code 10, which is why it can be printed as a char and counted like any other.

topics.title: getline keeps the spaces
topics.body: `std::getline` reads up to the delimiter, so a sentence survives intact where `>>` would have stopped at the first space.

topics.title: short and long have different widths
topics.body: The standard fixes minimum sizes, not exact ones, so `sizeof` is the honest way to report what this compiler chose.

topics.title: A literal suffix chooses its type
topics.body: `10u` is unsigned and `10L` is long, so the suffix changes the type and therefore the size the program sees.

topics.title: const cannot be reassigned
topics.body: A `const` variable is fixed after initialization; an assignment to it is a compile error rather than a silent change.

topics.title: Assignment can narrow a value
topics.body: Converting a `double` to `int` truncates toward zero and drops the fraction, which is a silent loss unless the code says otherwise.

topics.title: sizeof works on expressions
topics.body: The operand of `sizeof` is not evaluated; only its type matters, so `sizeof(3.14)` is the size of a double.

topics.title: Logical AND short-circuits
topics.body: When the left operand is false the right side is never evaluated, which is what makes `if (ptr && ptr->ok())` safe.

topics.title: Relational operators return bool
topics.body: A comparison produces a `bool`, so it can be printed, stored or combined without converting to int first.

topics.title: A left shift doubles the value
topics.body: Shifting left by n multiplies by two to the n, provided the result still fits in the type.

topics.title: Compound assignment combines two steps
topics.body: `x += 5` reads `x`, adds 5 and stores the result, which is exactly one mutation of the variable.

topics.title: The ternary returns one of two values
topics.body: Both branches must have compatible types, and only the chosen branch is evaluated.

topics.title: Nested if narrows a range
topics.body: Testing the broad range first and the narrow range inside it keeps each condition small and readable.

topics.title: default handles every other value
topics.body: A `default` label catches the values no case matched, so a switch over an open set still has a defined path.

topics.title: break leaves the whole switch
topics.body: Without `break` execution falls into the following cases; with it the switch ends immediately.

topics.title: Conditions combine with AND
topics.body: A compound condition expresses two requirements at once; both must be true before the branch runs.

topics.title: An if without braces takes one statement
topics.body: Braces are optional for a single statement, which is why adding a second line without braces changes the meaning.

topics.title: A while loop counts down
topics.body: The condition is checked before each pass, so a counter that reaches the limit ends the loop.

topics.title: A for loop can step by two
topics.body: The increment expression is arbitrary, so `i += 2` visits every second value without an extra condition.

topics.title: Nested loops make rows and columns
topics.body: The outer loop selects a row and the inner loop fills it, which is the shape behind every grid and pattern exercise.

topics.title: continue skips one iteration
topics.body: `continue` jumps to the next pass without ending the loop, which is how one value can be filtered out.

topics.title: An accumulator adds every value
topics.body: A variable declared before the loop and updated inside it carries the running total across iterations.

topics.title: A function returns one value
topics.body: The return type declares what the caller receives; returning early is how a function reports a result or a rejection.

topics.title: void means no return value
topics.body: A `void` function still performs work, as this one prints instead of returning a number.

topics.title: Parameters are copies by default
topics.body: Passing by value gives the function its own copy, so changing the parameter leaves the caller’s variable untouched.

topics.title: A function can call another
topics.body: Composing small functions keeps each one testable and lets a later change stay local.

topics.title: Overloads differ by parameter types
topics.body: The compiler picks the overload from the argument types, so the same name can serve an int and a string.
